text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The head of the Turkish navy says he is patiently waiting for the Islamist-led government to implement the decisions of the military-dominated National Security Council (MGK), which urged it to clamp down on Islamist activities.

- A private television channel has been ordered to shut down for three days by the television watchdog after broadcasting a secretly-filmed tape of a military doctor sexually harassing a young woman in his surgery.

- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist party and conservative main opposition blocked a draft law that would strip pump-action rifles of their status as hunting arms in order to crack down on their high sales.
- The Greek foreign minister, in an interview with a Turkish newspaper, calls for a reconciliation between old foes Greece and Turkey.
- An organised crime gang comprising of police, state-paid village guards, turncoat rebel Kurds and soldiers used trucks belonging to a state company to transport drugs.
- The Islamist Welfare Party is working hard on bringing its supporters into state offices now that it is in power as the senior partner in the coalition government.

- Two thousand people marched through Istanbul on Thursday to celebrate the Newroz festival, a traditional time for separatist unrest but which the government has increasingly tried to incorporate into the mainstream.
- Turkey's casinos could be closed down in six months' time if parliament votes in accordance with a decision by a commission of MPs recommending their total shut-down.
